MSME working capital

After this lesson you can:
  • Operate revolving limits and drawing power
  • Run stock statements, reviews and renewals

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page

  2. What a BA watches

  7. Knowledge check

1. The product

Not a loan but a revolving facility: an approved limit the business draws and repays continuously, paying interest daily on what it uses. The lender's real control is drawing power — the portion of the limit actually available, recalculated from the borrower's stock statements and receivables ageing after margins: current assets secure the facility, so available credit tracks their verified value.

Annual renewal re-underwrites the relationship; the facility never self-amortises, so review discipline substitutes for a repayment schedule.

2. What a BA watches

Stale stock statements are the classic decay: drawing power computed from six-month-old inventory data is fiction, and policy penalises late statements by cutting DP.

Stock audits verify the paper against the warehouse.

Continuous churn (deposits and draws) makes this the LMS's daily-interest, utilisation-math stress test — module 5's daily-reducing machinery in production.

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Utilisation-based interest and DP recalculation demand exact, auditable computation.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. The limit is ₹1 crore; margined stock and receivables support ₹62 lakh. How much can the borrower draw?

  1. ₹1 crore — the limit governs
  2. ₹62 lakh — drawing power binds inside the limit
  3. ₹81 lakh — the average
  4. Nothing until renewal
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Drawing power, recalculated from current-asset statements, is the operative ceiling; the sanctioned limit is only its upper bound.
